newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatia weekly - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatia weekly - July 30.

text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian weekly Globus. Reuters has not verifired these stories and does not vauch for their accuracy.

- Croatian Archbishop Alojzije Stepinac, who was tried and sentenced by communist Yugoslavia for allegedly collaborating with Croatian pro-Nazi regime in World War Two, in fact worked for British Intelligence Service. In Public Record Office in London, Globus found classified British documents dating from 1942, open for public after half a century.

- Hipocratus' oath prevents me from disclosing President Franjo Tudjman's bill of health. But medical team treating him stands behind its optimistic reports, says Health Minister Andrija Hebrang who claims Tudjman's healthy appeareance and outstanding intellectual activities dispute CNN allegations that the president has stomach cancer.
- Commentary: Is Tudjman really an anti-semite? The president under fire or how the only living statesman who fought with anti-fascists in World War Two now has a reputation of being a revisionist.

- Globus poll: Some 52.4 percent of Croatians think Tudjman does not hate Jews, opposed to 63.6 percent who thought the same in 1993. Some 12.9 percent of the polled think Jews hate Croatia, up from 11.4 in 1993.
-British journalist Marcus Tanner of The Independent, author of a book on Croatia, says he turned down The Hague tribunal's invitation to testify against Bosnian Croat general Tihomir Blaskic.
- Evidence on death fields in Bosnia -- not a single Moslem has been indicted for crimes committed against Bosnian Croats!

- Furious neighbours tore down the fence in front of tennis star Iva Majoli's villa, claiming the family was usurping public property. Globus described the event as one of the most brutal manifestation of petit-burgeois envy.

- Globus investigation of U.S. reports that Vatican hid gold of Croatian fascists, or ustashas in World War Two: Ustasha officer Srecko Rover tells the weekly how priest Krunoslav Draganovic took at least two cages full of Ustasha gold to Vatican.
